tasks.title: Add the pre-receive hook to the git server at the trunk-storer ref-write boundary
steps: Write TS-22-1 first, using newGitTestEnv and a real git push against the handler, and confirm it fails. It must prove that go-git turns a storer reference-write error into a per-ref 'ng' status that git shows as 'remote rejected'. Also confirm the real field names of packp.ReportStatus (UnpackStatus, CommandStatuses) and which storer method go-git calls (SetReference or CheckAndSetReference)

In internal/gitserver add the exported type PreReceiveHookFunc func(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, slug string, actor *apikit.AuthInfo, upd RefUpdate) error, a RefUpdate struct {Name plumbing.ReferenceName; Old, New plumbing.Hash}, and RegisterPreReceiveHook(fn) that stores a package-level hook (nil clears it) in the style of RegisterPostPushHook, guarded for concurrent access

Extend thinPackSafeStorer so it carries the request ctx, db, slug, actor and a hook lookup. Override SetReference, CheckAndSetReference and RemoveReference to call the hook once per update (new hash from the reference, old hash from the existing value or the CAS argument; zero hash for a removal) before delegating. A hook error is returned without touching the underlying storer. Keep hiding PackfileWriter

Make the loader and server per request, or otherwise bind the per-request context and actor from handleReceivePack (apikit.GetAuthInfo is nil-safe) into the storer wrapper. Keep info/refs, upload-pack and the existing loader behaviour unchanged
Record which refs the hook rejected on the request (a set keyed by ref name) so the accepted-refs logic in a later task can use it. With no hook registered the flow is identical to before
Make sure the empty-body no-op path never calls the hook and that no extra recover is added around the hook (a panic follows existing handler behaviour)
Write TS-22-2 to TS-22-8. TS-22-5 inspects 'go list -deps ./internal/gitserver' to prove it has no internal/carrypatch package; TS-22-6 posts a hand-built request without report-status
Confirm gitserver imports nothing from internal/carrypatch

tasks.title: Only accepted ref updates drive audit, post-push hook and rebuild
steps: Write TS-22-29, TS-22-30, TS-22-32 and TS-22-33 first and confirm they fail

Add a pure helper acceptedCommands(cmds []*packp.Command, rs *packp.ReportStatus, hookRejected map/set) []*packp.Command in internal/gitserver/handlers.go. With a report, a command is accepted only when its CommandStatuses entry (matched by ReferenceName) has Status ok. Without a report, it is accepted unless the pre-receive hook rejected it

In handleReceivePack, after ReceivePack, compute the accepted commands. Pass only them to emitGitPushAudit and to extractPushedBranches for the post-push hook. If none is accepted, emit no hub.git.push event and run no post-push hook. Deletes stay excluded from extractPushedBranches
Leave updateHeadSHA unchanged and still called for every push

Write TS-22-30 with a recording post-push hook and audit emitter and a push of p1 (hook-rejected), feature and a delete of old. Write TS-22-33 as a property test over generated commands and ok/error statuses using the classifier
TS-22-32 asserts head_sha equals the trunk HEAD after an accepted push and after a rejected-only push

Keep deps injectable so tests can stub the workspace, patches and variable lookups

tasks.title: Reject mode: refuse hub pushes to registered patch branches in origin mode
steps: Write TS-22-15 to TS-22-20 and TS-22-31 first and confirm they fail

In the carry-patch hook, when source is origin and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is not true, return errors.New("branch is synced from origin; push to "+sanitized git_url+" instead") for creates, updates and deletes of a registered patch branch

Add a stripUserinfo helper (net/url parse, clear User; fall back to a regexp removing user:password@ when the URL does not parse, including scp-like forms). Reuse it for later error sanitising. TS-22-17 is a property test over generated URLs, usernames and passwords with characters like ':' '%' '!'
Log each rejection at info level with slog fields slug, branch and user (apikit.AuthInfo user ID, or 'unknown' when actor is nil)

TS-22-31 uses the real post-push rebuild hook and a job queue to prove a rejected-only push enqueues no rebuild, emits no audit event and calls no hook

tasks.title: Forward mode: push to the fork before the hub writes its ref
steps: Write TS-22-21 to TS-22-28 first, using a local bare repository added as the trunk's origin remote, and confirm they fail

In the carry-patch hook, when source is origin and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is true: a delete of a registered branch returns 'branch is synced from origin; delete it on the fork instead' without contacting origin
For a create or update, resolve credentials with the injected resolver (workspace.ResolveCloneAuth wrapper); on error return exactly 'failed to resolve origin credentials' without contacting origin

Create the temporary ref refs/hub/forward/<branch> in the trunk pointing at the new commit (go-git PlainOpen of the trunk path; the workspace root comes from deps), push it via a seam around repo.PushContext with RemoteName origin, Force false, RefSpec 'refs/hub/forward/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>' with no '+', and a context.WithTimeout of 120 seconds. Treat git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate as success. Remove the temporary ref with defer on both success and failure
On failure return errors.New("origin rejected push: "+stripUserinfo(err.Error())), log at warn level with slug, branch, user and the sanitised error, and never accept silently

Check whether go-git supports a hash source; if not keep the temporary ref. Beware the hook runs inside the receive session, so opening the trunk via PlainOpen is a separate handle on the same on-disk repo; the new objects are already written
TS-22-23 asserts via the push seam: RemoteName origin, Force false, no leading '+', deadline about 120s, and that the resolver got the slug
TS-22-26 uses an unreachable origin URL containing user:pw@ and a captured slog handler and asserts no 'pw' appears in the client output or logs
TS-22-28 pushes a registered and an unregistered branch together and asserts the unregistered one is not on origin

tasks.title: Hub-mode mirror in the post-push hook and the hub.patch.mirror_failed event
steps: Write the listed tests first and confirm they fail
In internal/audit/types.go add the constant EventPatchMirrorFailed = "hub.patch.mirror_failed" directly next to EventRebuildFollowup

Extend NewPostPushRebuildHook in internal/carrypatch/push_hook.go with new dependencies: an origin credentials resolver, a workspace root and an audit emitter. Keep existing call sites compiling (variadic options or extra params; update push_hook_test.go callers). Any nil/empty dependency disables the mirror and leaves rebuild behaviour as before

After the rebuild enqueue (always executed first, whether enqueued, suppressed by AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH=false, deduplicated or failed) run mirrorBranches in the same goroutine: skip unless workspace is carry_patch, PATCH_PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is the exact string true and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE resolves to hub (reuse the applicability code from push_control.go: registered, non-deleted, not integration branch)

For each applicable branch resolve credentials, open the trunk with git.PlainOpen, and PushContext with RemoteName origin, RefSpec '+refs/heads/<n>:refs/heads/<n>', Force true semantics through the refspec, a 120 second timeout and NoErrAlreadyUpToDate as success. A failure of one branch does not stop the others; there is no retry or persistence

On success log at info. On failure log at warn with slug, branch and the error with userinfo removed (reuse stripUserinfo) and emit audit.HubEvent with the new type, resource_type patch, action mirror, actor_type system, the slug and metadata {branch_name, error}. A nil emitter skips emission; an emit error is only logged
